title: Orchestrate synthetic workloads and prune harness dependencies
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Our synthetic workload orchestration and perf regression harness have accumulated multiple small hacks and heavyweight transitive dependencies (old grpc stubs, a forked seq-generator, and a deprecated timer wheel). This makes local iteration slow, CI runs brittle, and increases flakiness in long-tail latency tests. Goal: refactor the harness to a lightweight orchestration layer with a declarative workload spec, remove or replace obsolete deps, and add clear migration shims so existing scenario specs continue to work without rewrites. Scope: 1) introduce a minimal workload coordinator that normalizes scheduling, timeout, and retry semantics; 2) replace the forked seq-generator with a drop-in seeded iterator that supports deterministic replay; 3) migrate off the deprecated timer-wheel lib to a small internal token-bucket implementation; 4) shrink the test harness docker image by removing unused language runtimes and large devtools; 5) add guardrails in CI to prevent reintroducing removed deps.
acceptance_criteria: 1) CI regression suite (smoke+long-tail) completes within target time budget on the new harness (<= 30% of previous median runtime) and flakiness rate reduces by >= 40% over 30 runs; 2) No runtime compatibility break for existing scenario specs (backwards shim passes existing goldens); 3) Docker image size reduced by at least 180MB; 4) Removed or replaced transitive deps documented and PRs merged; 5) New coordinator exposes metrics for scheduling, queue depth, and per-scenario latency to the perf dashboard.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): prototype coordinator that replays a single scenario deterministically and replaces timer-wheel. Artifacts: minimal coordinator binary, benchmark comparing old vs new timing semantics. Phase 2 (refactor, 2 weeks): implement seeded iterator replacement, integrate coordinator into CI smoke runner, add metrics exporter. Phase 3 (cutover, 1 week): run dual-run experiments in a canary job, compare goldens, flip default runner for perf-regression job. Phase 4 (cleanup, 1 week): prune deps from image, update docs, add CI gate preventing reintroduction of removed packages.
risks: Some older scenario specs rely on undefined timing side-effects and may diverge under deterministic scheduling
Third-party replacement libs may have hidden edge cases for large-batch scenarios
Image size reduction could remove tools relied on by local debug flows — will mitigate with a debug image target
notes:
- Decision: prefer small in-repo implementation for the timer/token-bucket to avoid another external dependency.
- We will keep a compatibility shim layer that translates legacy scenario fields to new spec fields during the transition.
- Measured baseline runtimes: median full-regression run = 42m, 95th percentile latency flakiness ~ 18%.
- Target metrics exported: harness.run_duration_seconds, harness.queue_depth, harness.skipped_retries_total.
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PERF/Coordinator+Design (internal).
